📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 03:16 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 06:39 EST, 26 November 2026.

Joshua Kimmich has hammered his own club Bayern Munich for their 'incomprehensible' and 'unacceptable' undermining of Jamal Musiala's ongoing illness battle.

Musiala, the 23-year-old golden boy of German football, has hardly played this season due to seizures brought on by 'neurological dysfunction' and has an £18m-a-year salary until 2030.

Last week, Bayern board member Karl-Heinz Rummenigge suggested the club could discuss him taking a pay cut, arguing: 'We need to talk to the family, the player, and the agency, because then these sums of money, sorry, with all due respect, are no longer feasible.

‘I cannot imagine that Jamal wants to leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions.'.

There was a huge outcry after Rummenigge's remarks, with the likes of Jude Bellingham, Michael Olise and Rio Ferdinand all backing Musiala.

It has been revealed that and when asked about the situation after Bayern's 2-1 defeat by Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday night, Kimmich noted: 'What happened now is something that simply must never happen in this way. I find it completely incomprehensible.

Joshua Kimmich hammered Bayern Munich for their handling of Jamal Musiala's situation.

Musiala came off the bench for Bayern in their 2-1 defeat by Lille on Wednesday night.

In a recent development, 'I think this is something that should be discussed behind closed doors, something you can address with Jamal's agent or with Jamal himself. And I think the other side is open to that as well.

According to recent reports, 'I believe I've also read that they've met and are supposed to issue a statement. What I don't understand is the way this is being communicated publicly. It must never happen that a player is made to bear the brunt of it.

Industry observers note that 'Of course, the club always comes first and is bigger than us as players, but it's not bigger than the person. And that's an absolute no-go. It's also not the Bayern way. Especially at this particular time, when I've often emphasised how special this club is.

Recent findings suggest that 'Even in my own situation, the club was incredibly special. You could really feel that this sense of togetherness was being lived out.'.

Kimmich pointed out that Musiala's health complications are in no way a result of him being unprofessional.

'We mustn't forget that he underwent another operation in the summer and then suffered another injury afterwards,' he continued.

'But I see him and spend time with him every day. I see how he works and how hard he works. That's another key aspect of the situation. It's not as though he's having problems because he's unprofessional. Quite the opposite: he's here every day, naturally wants to get the very best out of himself, works extremely hard every day and, I think, genuinely enjoys being part of our team.

'I hope he knows that all of us are 100% behind him, both the team and the club officials.'.

While Kimmich offered his support to Musiala, he admitted he did understand the difficulty the club faces financially with one of their most expensive players unable to start more than one Bundesliga game this season.

Musiala collapsed on the pitch at two consecutive games in August (pictured being helped by team-mates against RB Leipzig).

According to recent reports, he continued: 'Generally speaking, you have to look at the situation from different perspectives. I have absolute understanding for the fact that this is not an easy situation for a club either.

According to recent reports, 'Of course, I've witnessed Jamal's journey over the past two years. I mean, he carried us at the Euros and was our standout player afterwards. Then he signed a contract extension, was given the number 10 shirt here and with the German national team. Then came the first muscle injury. I can speak from personal experience: when you extend your contract, especially at that age, it's not about sitting back and enjoying the next five years.

Recent findings suggest that 'Rather, it's a source of motivation and a responsibility you want to live up to. Then Jamal had the illness and the serious injury. We mustn't forget that over the past year and a half, I don't think he's managed to play four or five games in a row.

'So it's understandable to some extent that he's not performing at his usual level. And it's also understandable that the club might be concerned because of the illness.'.

The Germany international was diagnosed over the summer with absence seizures, a form of epilepsy which causes 'brief but easily treatable seizures'.

Musiala shocked the sporting world when he collapsed in two matches earlier this season, with Bayern manager Vincent Kompany explaining that the player had suffered from a reaction to a change in his medication.

Honorary president Uli Hoeness was the first to speak out on the potential drop-off in form Musiala might suffer with long-term absences, claiming earlier this month that he 'may never regain the performance level he once had'.

'We are facing a dilemma in this case, as he is suffering from an illness that cannot simply be cured, but it can be controlled to a certain extent with the use of medication,' Hoeness told German outlet BR24.

Both Uli Hoeness and Karl-Heinz Rummenigge have made comments suggesting consequences should Musiala not return to his level.

Chief executive Jan-Christian Dreesen then backed up Hoeness's comments and implied that Musiala's contract may need to be 'assessed'.

Sources indicate that 'We're monitoring his level of play. He'll certainly need time to improve further – like any injured player,' Dreesen mentioned in discussion with AZ. 'And then we need to calmly assess the situation and, if necessary, sit down with his family and management.

'Either we'll all be happy together and he'll be the same Jamal he always was – or, if he's a different Jamal along the way, we'll have to discuss it.'.

'If we're not consistently at a level that also aligns with the economic realities, then we'll have to talk to each other. Nevertheless, we have a valid contract, and that's the end of it.'.

The 23-year-old is one of Bayern's highest-earners, having signed a deal with the club to extend his time in Bavaria in February 2025.

Adding fuel to the fire days later was former CEO Karl-Heinz Rummenigge, who told Sky Sports/RTL that he thought it was almost reasonable to discuss a renegotiation should Musiala not return to the level at which he once played.

But the player union Fifpro were forthright in their disagreement with his statements,  releasing a statement claiming that all parties presently sharing their views on Musiala's contract 'should know better'.

'Bayern's honorary president, chief executive and former chief executive have all publicly questioned Musiala's contract in quick succession,' the statement read.

It has been revealed that 'In Fifpro's view, this is a co-ordinated strategy to put pressure on Musiala and his representatives ahead of any negotiations. A club of Bayern's standing should know better.'.

When this statement was shared to social media via journalist Fabrizio Romano, global talents including Jude Bellingham and Musiala's team-mate Michael Olise were among those to like the post.

Criticisms were even more fiery in Germany, with the vice president of Germany's player union Michael Franz accusing the club of harassment.

'What the Bayern Munich officials are doing, and I don't mean Kompany and (Max) Eberl (director of sport), who have behaved impeccably, seems despicable to me,' Franz shared in an interview with Sport1. 'There is even something about it that resembles harassment.'.

'A footballer's level of performance can be discussed publicly, but it is not right to talk about his illness and the salary he receives in such circumstances. We must not forget that Jamal Musiala has done everything in his power to come back.'.

'Money has become more crucial than the person, and that is unacceptable.'.

Musiala collapsed twice within four days in mid-August, first during Bayern's match against Leipzig – shortly after scoring – and then against Heidenheim.

He then returned to the pitch in September, netting against Bodo/Glimt in Champions League action and Union Berlin shortly before the first international break.

After suffering a hamstring injury, Musiala then spent time away from the side before his return at the end of last week – a match which also saw Harry Kane suffer an ankle injury which will keep him out for over three months.

Musiala came off the bench on Wednesday night against Lille and managed to play the final 15 minutes of the 2-1 defeat.

Quantum-enhanced sensing with 500 photons via Fock-space confocal focusing

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2527 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1,2,3,4,5,6,7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10,11,12.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Quantum metrology promises measurement precision beyond classical limits by exploiting large-scale quantum states1,2,3,4,5,6,7, yet realizing this advantage faces two fundamental challenges: the deterministic preparation of non-trivial quantum probes8,9 and the efficient extraction of metrological information in high-dimensional Hilbert spaces10,11,12. Here, we introduce quantum confocal microscopy in Fock space that addresses these challenges for a Fock-like probe state with a tightly concentrated photon-number distribution. Drawing a direct analogy between classical wave optics and quantum state evolution in a bosonic mode13,14, we construct a confocal lens system with a quantum circuit of \({\mathcal{O}}(1)\) operational depth, realizing a bidirectional transformation between a readily obtainable coherent state and this Fock-like probe state. Using a superconducting circuit quantum electrodynamics platform, we deterministically prepare focused probe states with mean photon numbers up to N = 500, achieving a 21.5 ± 1.1 dB reduction of the photon-number variance relative to a coherent state. Using the focused states for displacement sensing, we achieve a record metrological gain of 19.20 ± 0.20 dB beyond the standard quantum limit. This work establishes quantum confocal microscopy as a compact protocol that makes high-photon-number non-Gaussian Fock-like probes experimentally accessible and measurable, providing a viable route towards quantum-enhanced precision measurement, and is readily extendable to other bosonic platforms and high-dimensional quantum many-body systems.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mauricio Pochettino has been urged to consider making the first ruthless decision of his Manchester United tenure in the wake of last night’s 2-2 draw against Sporting Lisbon.

Having trailed at half-time, the Red Devils looked on course for a morale-boosting victory following a quickfire Bruno Fernandes brace.

The United captain equalised from the penalty spot, before scoring an outrageous fluke when an innocuous looking shot hit a divot and flew beyond the grasp of a bamboozled Kaique Pereira.

Any suggestion that fortune had turned for Pochettino’s ailing side, however, was dispelled with 10 minutes remaining when Senne Lammens made his second inexplicable error of the game by dropping a routine cross and gifting Luis Suarez a goal from close range.

The Belgium international was signed 18 months ago Royal Antwerp and initially looked to have solved United’s long-standing goalkeeping matter.

Lammens is now, however, making mistakes at a similar rate to that of his predecessor, the hapless Andre Onana, and Jamie Carragher believes taking the confidence-starved 24-year-old out of the limelight for the spell would represent a sensible course of action for Pochettino.

Delivering his verdict on Lammens’ performance, Carragher said on CBS: ‘You worry about the confidence of that goalkeeper now.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

In a recent development, ‘That mistake for the equaliser, the 2-2 goal, you say sometimes ‘an amateur goalkeeper wouldn’t make that mistake’. If that was an amateur goalkeeper you’d be thinking ‘that can’t happen’. That just can’t happen at this level.

‘It is getting to the stage with the goalkeeper now. The focus on a Man Utd goalkeeper is always significant if he’s making mistakes. I don’t think the back-up’s even at the level where, no matter how poorly the goalkeeper plays, you change it.’.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

Pochettino has the experience Karl Darlow, signed from Leeds United in the summer, to call upon but the fresh United boss was keen to back Lammens last night following his latest disastrous display.

Sources indicate that pochettino remarked: ‘That is football. Football is about making mistakes. I always want to support my players. It’s something that happened in that case. I think we need to talk about responsibility and it’s our responsibility too to provide the best tools.

‘I think in this type of action, our defensive line also needs to cover the keeper better because it was very difficult. It’s not to blame the defensive line, but it’s two things that we need to improve, details that we need to work on.

It has been revealed that ‘Professional players need to refresh concepts, refresh details until that becomes a habit. And I think things that we need to improve are habits in a defensive way, offensive way, in all the areas.

Industry observers note that ‘It’s to blame us because I think we need to manage this type of situation better, because this situation, when you are a keeper, is not easy and you always need help from your teammates. But of course, we accept the challenge and we are here to try to improve the small details – for sure we will improve.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Bayern Munich will hope to arrest their troubles by getting the better of hosts Hamburger SV at Volksparkstadion on Saturday and reclaim top spot in the Bundesliga table.
  • The Bavarians are second with 22 points in the league, so they will need Borussia Dortmund to avoid winning in order to climb to first, whereas the home side are 12th with 12 points.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 26 Nov 2026 23:19, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:12.

Bayern Munich will hope to arrest their troubles by getting the better of hosts Hamburger SV at Volksparkstadion on Saturday and reclaim top spot in the Bundesliga table.

The Bavarians are second with 22 points in the league, so they will need Borussia Dortmund to avoid winning in order to climb to first, whereas the home side are 12th with 12 points.

Hamburger's campaign has been positive, especially as they have taken three more points after 10 matchweeks this season than they did at the same stage in 2025-26.

The club did lose 4-0 against Werder Bremen on November 22, and a defeat on the weekend could leave them just two points above the bottom three.

Head coach Daniel Thioune will be alarmed that his side have lost four of their last five games in all competitions, with the club scoring five goals while conceding on 12 occasions.

The Green-Whites' next task is to get the better of Bayern for the first time since July 2011, a period in which they suffered 17 defeats and drew three times.

HSV's record as hosts has been commendable this term considering they have triumphed in three of their five league outings at Volksparkstadion, though they were beaten twice in that stretch.

Bayern are in the unusual position of having to bounce back from a loss after Lille won 2-1 against them in the Champions League on Wednesday.

That was Vincent Kompany's second game on the touchline following his collapse in October, but his first match back was hardly better, with his side drawing 1-1 with FC Koln on November 20.

The visitors are only two points behind first-placed Borussia Dortmund, but with numerous injuries throughout the squad, there are fears that the gap could widen.

Injuries and form are not the only problems plaguing the champions, whose hierarchy have come under fire for their handling of Jamal Musiala's health situation, prompting Joshua Kimmich to speak up in support of the attacker.

Nevertheless, it should not be forgotten that the Bavarians have scored 30 goals in 10 top-flight games, while only Dortmund have conceded fewer goals than their 10.

Bayern's defeat against Lille was their first in any competition this campaign, and it was also their first away defeat, with the visitors having won six and drawn three of their first nine away fixtures of the season.

Hamburger SV form (all competitions):.

Bayern Munich form (all competitions):.

Hamburger midfielder Nicolai Remberg has been ruled out for the rest of the season, meaning the hosts may have to rely upon Nicolas Capaldo in the middle of the pitch.

With striker Yussuf Poulsen unavailable, Patson Daka will be expected to lead the line, and he may be supported by Fabio Vieira.

Bayern will be without Harry Kane for months due to an ankle injury, and to make matters worse, Michael Olise is a doubt.

Luis Diaz should be ready to feature in some capacity on the weekend, though he faces the prospect of playing in a forward line led by natural midfielder Konrad Laimer.

Aleksandar Pavlovic played in an advanced role against Lille due to injuries in attack, but he should be able to return to a deeper role alongside Kimmich.

Hamburger SV possible starting lineup:.

Fernandes; Nandja, Bornauw, Omari; El Ouahdi, Adeline, Capaldo, Gronbaek, Wolfe; Daka, Vieira.

Bayern Munich possible starting lineup:.

Urbig; Stanisic, Upamecano, Tah, Ito; Kimmich, Pavlovic; Diaz, Karl, Brown; Laimer.

Hamburger may never have a better opportunity than now to take points from Bayern, who have several key absentees.

However, Bayern still boast immense quality in their squad, and they should still be able to come out on top, even if the match is far from straightforward.

David Raya injury enhancement as expert explains if Arsenal star can play against Man City

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Arsenal hope David Raya has avoided a serious shoulder injury but their goalkeeper is still likely to be a doubt for Sunday’s Premier League showdown against Manchester City.
  • The Spain international injured his shoulder in a rather innocuous incident during last weekend’s draw with Newcastle United, making contact with William Osula while claiming a cross.
  • In a recent development, raya was left in considerable pain with Sky Sports forced to apologise for initially playing down the incident.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Arsenal hope David Raya has avoided a serious shoulder injury but their goalkeeper is still likely to be a doubt for Sunday’s Premier League showdown against Manchester City.

The Spain international injured his shoulder in a rather innocuous incident during last weekend’s draw with Newcastle United, making contact with William Osula while claiming a cross.

In a recent development, raya was left in considerable pain with Sky Sports forced to apologise for initially playing down the incident. The former Brentford star trudged off the pitch clutching his arm to be replaced by Kepa Arrizabalaga, who started in his place in the Champions League against Borussia Dortmund on Tuesday night.

Sources indicate that raya was visibly distressed on Saturday night and it prompted huge concerns over the man who has been so pivotal to Arsenal’s rise to the summit of English football. While boasting the most formidable squad in the Premier League, Raya is simply irreplaceable.

The outlook was brighter this week with Mikel Arteta revealing his goalkeeper will not require surgery.

‘We expected something much worse because he could almost not handle the amount of pain he had in that moment,’ Arteta told the media earlier this week.

Recent findings suggest that ‘The first tests that we have done have shown something that is much more encouraging. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let’s see.’.

Arsenal have not disclosed any specific details over the injury but it seems clear at this stage Raya is not facing the sort of layoff that kept Nick Pope out for over four months after he suffered a dislocated shoulder in 2023.

They will hope any layoff is a short-term one heading into the festive period with a trip to the Etihad now looming large this weekend. Kepa was trusted with a starting role against City in the Carabao Cup final ahead of Raya back in March, having started in every previous round of the competition, but was at fault at Wembley that day as Pep Guardiola’s side claimed the first silverware of the season.

Recent findings suggest that there was plenty of panic on Saturday night as Raya made his way off the pitch at St James’ Park. While Bukayo Saka, Declan Rice, William Saliba, Gabriel Magalhaes are pivotal figures, there is simply no replacing their no1.

Pundits lined up fearing the worst for Arsenal at the weekend with Jamie Redknapp suggesting any absence will ‘change everything for Arsenal for a while.’.

Read more on what he and Arsenal legend Ian Wright said on the night.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

While Arteta trusts Kepa, getting Raya back as soon as possible will be vital. Arsenal have sent reassuring messages this week but having him back in time for this weekend is likely to be a significant ask.

‘It is so hard to tell how long he may be out for, we would want to know the full diagnosis,’ Stephen Smith, CEO and founder of Kitman Labs which specialises in injury welfare and performance analytics, told Metro.

Sources indicate that ‘All we have to use is the replay of the incident and how he looked coming off the pitch and he did look in incredible pain. He looked like someone who had dislocated his shoulder playing rugby. My guess is that if there was that much pain and discomfort immediately, this weekend would be too soon. That said, looking back at how innocuous it was, you would hope the length of his absence  would be the small number of weeks range.’.

Arsenal have a relatively clean bill of health elsewhere in the squad with Martin Zubimendi and Bukayo Saka their only other absences.

Saka’s latest injury is likely to keep him out until Christmas with spells on the sidelines becoming increasingly regular for the winger.

Saka sidelined agai (Picture: Getty).

Are a growing number of knocks coupled with the years of unrelenting game time taking their toll on the England international?

Read our deep dive into Saka’s injury history as the experts tell us if Arsenal have something to really be concerned with.

Arsenal sit six points clear at the top of the league and don’t play a game outside of London until mid-January. But their run of fixtures in December could provide the most thorough examination of their ability to defend their crown this season.

Industry observers note that the month starts with a trip to Raya’s old club Brentford, followed by the north London derby against a rejuvenated Tottenham. Real Madrid then come to town in the Champions League before Arsenal host Bournemouth, who walked away with the win on their last visit to north London. They then host Manchester United in their last game before Christmas.

Arteta will be expected to shed more light on Raya’s recovery period when he speaks to the press on Friday with he and his staff now likely to have a clear picture of what the injury is after further scans this week.

Raya is perhaps the most athletic goalkeeper in the league and ensuring he is able to reach his spectacular physical levels will be key in the coming days and weeks.

Smith explained the process will involve four stages to ensure Raya is pain-free before he returns to action.

‘Finding out surgery is not needed so quickly was very encouraging. My guess is after the second scan this week they will know exactly what it is at this point,’ he remarked.

Sources indicate that ‘In terms of recovery time, it all depends on exactly what it is. If it was a slight subluxation then they will be looking at letting that rest, recover and become pain free, allowing it to get a range of motion back before doing a small amount of strengthening work and get him back out there.

It has been revealed that ‘If it something closer to a rotator cuff strain it may take a little longer. Typically what they are looking at in this situation comes in four stages. The first is settling the pain and protecting the joint, the second is getting full range back, the third is rebuilding strength around it and fourth, which can take a bit more time, is position-specific loading.

‘When you think about the shoulder and what a goalkeeper is required to do – all their diving and landing, catching overhead, distributing the ball – it’s pretty demanding on the shoulder. So even if it is on the lower end of the scale from a structural damage perspective, it is still likely to require time to make sure he is capable of doing all that.

It has been revealed that ‘The first 48 hours will have been the most painful. But throughout the rehab process, they won’t want him to be sore. If he’s sore, that means potentially they aren’t giving it enough time. So they will want him to feel really comfortable and really strong.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Nsidibe Akpan | 26 Nov 2026 23:24, Last updated: 27 Nov 2026 10:10.

SBV Excelsior host SC Telstar at Stadion Woudestein in Rotterdam in round 14 of the 2026-27 Eredivisie on Saturday with kick-off at 3.30pm GMT.

Excelsior and Telstar drew 2-2 at BUKO Stadion on November 1, 2025 and again at Stadion Woudestein on January 17, 2026, but the Kralingers now sit 13th on 14 points, four clear of the relegation play-off place that De Witte Leeuwen occupy on 10.

Ruben den Uil's Excelsior ended a run of five straight league defeats with a 3-2 win at Feyenoord on November 21, their first league victory at De Kuip since 1980.

After Givairo Read gave Feyenoord a lead on two minutes, Mario Dominguez levelled on six, Irakli Yegoian scored a penalty on 40 and Casper Widell headed in from a corner on 58.

Jan Plug, who is on loan from Feyenoord, turned the ball into his own net on 67 minutes, but the visitors held on.

Excelsior had 10 points from their first five games, including a 4-0 win at Cambuur on the opening day, then took one point from the next seven.

The low point came on November 1, when Twente won 9-0 at Woudestein, the heaviest league defeat in the club's history, with Nesto Groen sent off after five minutes.

A 1-0 home loss to Go Ahead Eagles on November 7 left Excelsior without a league goal in four games, and they had conceded 20 times in five league matches before the Feyenoord win, leaving a goal difference of -12 from 13 games.

Henk Brugge, in his first permanent head coach job after succeeding Anthony Correia in May, has Telstar 16th on the Eredivisie table with 10 points from two wins, four draws and seven defeats, with 19 goals scored and 28 conceded.

Telstar went ahead after 16 minutes against PEC Zwolle on November 21 through a Simon Graves own goal, but Dylan Mbayo scored twice before half time and Ibrahim Cissoko added a third after a poor back pass from Gabi Caschili.

That 3-1 home defeat means Telstar have gone 17 matches without beating Zwolle in all competitions, and Brugge admitted afterwards that his side may have played the better football but defended badly at key moments.

Telstar have scored in each of their last six league games, 14 goals in all, but they conceded 16 across those matches, including a 4-2 win over Utrecht and 2-2 draws with ADO Den Haag and at Fortuna Sittard.

The defence is the problem at BUKO Stadion, where Telstar have conceded 20 goals in seven league games this season.

Away from Velsen-Zuid, Telstar have taken one point from their last three league trips, losing 1-0 at AZ Alkmaar and 3-2 at Go Ahead Eagles before the 2-2 draw at Fortuna Sittard, and Tyrone Owusu leads the team with five goals this season.

SBV Excelsior form (all competitions):.

Telstar form (all competitions):.

Excelsior have no reported injuries or suspensions, with Groen available again after serving his ban by missing the Go Ahead Eagles game and the trip to Feyenoord.

Sliti, who has three league goals, feared a bruised or broken thumb after Netherlands Under-21s duty on November 17 but started at De Kuip, so Alireza Jahanbakhsh and David Garden remain options from the bench.

Noah Naujoks is back in the midfield after a long injury absence and started alongside Lennard Hartjes, who has suffered three cruciate ligament tears in his career, two of them at Excelsior.

Telstar have no confirmed absentees, with Gerald Alders and Rui Mendes both returning from injury as substitutes against Zwolle, on 57 and 84 minutes respectively.

Nokkvi Thorisson and Jeff Hardeveld, who both came on after 57 minutes against Zwolle, are options to start in attack.

SBV Excelsior possible starting lineup:.

Van Gassel; Bos, Plug, Widell, Meissen; Naujoks, Hartjes, Yegoian; Sliti, Dominguez, Thorsteinsson.

Telstar possible starting lineup:.

Koeman Jr; Peersman, Soualhia, Valk, Caschili; Rossen, Ahmed; Martha, Owusu, Demircan; Brouwer.

Excelsior revealed at Feyenoord that the goals have returned, with a side that had scored once in five league games finding the net three times against the division's second-highest scoring attack, including a Widell header from a corner and a Dominguez finish after a midfield giveaway.

Telstar have scored in six straight league games, so a clean sheet is unlikely for an Excelsior defence that has conceded 31 times in 13 matches, but Telstar have taken one point from their last three away games and let in 20 goals in seven home league games, which suggests their backline will struggle with Dominguez and Sliti.

The counter-argument is the 9-0 Twente result, yet that came with Groen sent off after five minutes, while the draws in both meetings last season show Telstar can score at Woudestein, so Excelsior should edge a match in which both sides concede.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Sebastian Sternik | 26 Nov 2026 23:26.

FC Koln will be looking to end their five-game winless run in the Bundesliga when they welcome newly promoted Elversberg to the RheinEnergieStadion on Saturday afternoon.

The Billy Goats will take confidence from their impressive draw against Bayern Munich, while the visitors arrive having lost five of their last seven matches across all competitions.

Frustration has been a recurring theme throughout Koln’s first 10 league games, with Rene Wagner’s side sitting just three points clear of the bottom three despite losing only four times.

Several sides above them in the table have suffered more defeats, but Koln’s joint-high number of draws has prevented them from making a serious push up the Bundesliga standings.

However, their 1-1 draw away to Bayern Munich at the Allianz Arena last Friday night was certainly one point worth celebrating.

The Billy Goats ended their six-match losing run against the bruised German champions, and allowed Borussia Dortmund to reclaim top spot in the Bundesliga.

Buoyed by that performance, Koln will now be targeting their first league victory since early October, which would bring an end to their five-game winless run in the competition.

The hosts will be further encouraged by the fact they won three of their six home games across all competitions this season, scoring 12 goals along the way.

Since collecting seven points from their opening four Bundesliga matches, Elversberg have begun to discover just how difficult life in Germany’s top flight can be.

Representing a town with a population of around 13,000, the newly promoted side were always likely to face an uphill battle against German football’s biggest clubs.

Their recent form has underlined the scale of that challenge, with Elversberg suffering five defeats in their last seven matches across all competitions.

On a slight positive note, all but one of those losses have come by a single-goal margin - a stat which demonstrates just how competitive the Black and Whites have been.

That narrow pattern continued in their most recent games, as Vincent Wagner’s side endured a 2-1 defeat to Borussia Dortmund before losing 1-0 to Freiburg last Saturday.

Despite that latest setback, Wagner believes his men delivered their best defensive performance of the season, restricting Freiburg to just one shot on target.

Results may have dipped, but the supporters have continued to show their backing, with around 5,000 expected to make the trip to Cologne - almost 40% of the entire population of the town.

Meanwhile, Wagner has already hinted that the club could explore the January transfer market, with sporting director Christian Weber understood to have a recruitment plan in mind.

Elversberg form (all competitions):.

Koln have one or two selection concerns heading into Saturday’s clash, mainly regarding the availability of Ragnar Ache.

The 28-year-old has been sidelined with a thigh injury since the start of October and, despite returning to training five weeks ago, is yet to make an appearance.

Head coach Wagner described Ache as “fit, training and eager”, although his lack of match action continues to leave a massive question mark around his name.

Fellow striker Thijs Dallinga is a more definite absentee, having been ruled out for the remainder of the season with a torn cruciate ligament.

This means that Wagner could turn to either Marius Bulter or Malek El Mala to lead the attacking efforts alongside Stated El Mala.

There are also concerns over captain and goalkeeper Marvin Schwabe, who landed awkwardly during last Friday’s draw with Bayern Munich and missed training on Monday and Tuesday due to back pain.

Veteran keeper Ron-Robert Zieler could replace him, though it is worth noting that the 2014 World Cup winner has not tasted competitive action in a little over 12 months.

When it comes to Elversberg, the visitors are almost injury-free, with the exception of Nicholas Mickelson, who returned from international duty with a knee problem.

There are also slight doubts over the availability of Lasse Gunther and Nicolas Kristof, who are both struggling with colds.

Noah Darvich, who is suffering from muscular problems, is a doubt and a decision over his availability could be made as late as Saturday morning.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • City started the season in fine form after Enzo Maresca’s arrival, but have now slipped to third and are without a win in their last four league matches.
  • Last season’s runners-up spent lavishly over the summer, but now trail Arsenal by six points ahead of their pivotal meeting at the Emirates on Sunday.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Lee Dixon thinks Manchester City’s Premier League title chances are far from over even if they fall to defeat against Arsenal on Sunday.

City started the season in fine form after Enzo Maresca’s arrival, but have now slipped to third and are without a win in their last four league matches.

Last season’s runners-up spent lavishly over the summer, but now trail Arsenal by six points ahead of their pivotal meeting at the Emirates on Sunday.

Bubbling away in the background remains the possibility of a huge points deduction after the club were found guilty of all but one of the 115 charges for financial breaches.

And Dixon believes that such uncertainty might be playing on the minds of City’s players, telling Metro: ‘Nobody liked Arsenal under George Graham and we built up resilience because of that.

‘I think that could have been happening for City at the start of the season with the charges, but that bounce can die off a bit and then all of a sudden, you’ve had a couple of bad results and it gets into your head.’.

Arsenal could extend their lead over City to nine points with victory at the Emirates on Sunday, but Dixon believes that it would still be far too early to rule City out of this season’s title race.

‘As a fan, after seeing Arsenal get over the line last season, you now have something to fall back on and I do believe that, from a fan’s perspective, if you see Arsenal beat City on Sunday, you can think that’s it,’ he added.

Sources indicate that ‘However, as a player, you won’t see any of them coming out and going, “It’s done and dusted”, because City have so much quality. We all know that City could go on a ten-game winning streak, so they’ll always have that opportunity.

Use AI to go deeper into the stories you care about – powered by Metro and trusted publications.

‘At the moment, there’s less pressure for Arsenal at the top from a points perspective and it’s pointing to it being their title to lose, but right now, it’s too early in the season to say it’s over if Arsenal win on Sunday.’.

Arsenal have not been at their best since returning from the international break, with a draw against Newcastle last weekend followed up by a stalemate against Borussia Dortmund in midweek.

But Dixon has still been encouraged by some aspects of Arsenal’s football, most notably the performances of Noni Madueke, who has featured more prominently since Bukayo Saka sustained a thigh injury last month.

‘I love his directness because when he comes on, his first touch is generally in the direction of the full-back which is what I hated as a full-back myself,’ Dixon said of Madueke.

Industry observers note that ‘You know what you’re in for as a full-back coming up against somebody like him. I’ve been very impressed with him but I’ve always been worried by his end product, but he seems to be producing better numbers now.

‘You need to take your hat off to him for that because Saka’s boots are big boots to fill. He’s really had to knuckle down and he’s receiving the benefit of that.’.

Lee Dixon was speaking with Metro on behalf of Betfred.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Crystal Palace delivered Thomas Frank a first victory after they came back to beat 10-man Real Sociedad 2-1 in the Europa League.

Dean Henderson was kept busy in the first half, making several stops to ensure it was all to play for after the break in south London, where Frank took charge of a home game for the first time.

Mamadou Sarr broke the deadlock in the 66th minute, but the contest turned on its head when Jon Martin was sent off with a second yellow card six minutes later.

Jean-Philippe Mateta fired in the penalty before second-half substitute Dwight McNeil tapped home from Jorgen Strand Larsen’s overhead kick.

Yeremy Pino had a chance to put the game away with a stoppage-time penalty but he was denied by Unai Marrero, and the hosts had to grind out a nervy finish.

The result moves the Eagles into a play-off position, after starting the evening just outside of it, in 25th.

Frank once again elected to employ a back four, as he did in his first game in charge, their 3-2 Premier League loss at Coventry.

The first chance came after a cagey first 10 minutes when the hosts gave the ball away and it fell to Benat Turrientes, who drew Henderson into a save from distance.

Henderson was then called back into action, twice denying the ever-threatening Goncalo Guedes, who was teed up by Mikel Oyarzabal’s through ball.

Palace’s best opportunity came on the stroke of half-time via a Richards throw-in, glanced on by Axel Disasi and nodded over by Mateta.

Crystal Palace handed WSL points deduction after illegal substitution.

The hosts were lucky not to concede five minutes after the restart, Guedes once again at the heart of it when he laid the ball on a plate for Oyarzabal, who was one-on-one with Henderson about eight yards out but fired straight at the Eagles keeper.

Henderson made his fifth save of the night, reacting promptly to deny Jon Gorrotxategi, and the visitors remained in the driver’s seat as the hour approached and Frank made his first substitution, replacing Eddie Nketiah with McNeil.

The breakthrough for Sociedad was the product of a patient build-up ending in Job Ochieng’s low pass for Sarr, who tapped it home.

The sides were level six minutes later. Palace were awarded a penalty after Martin – who was shown a second yellow card – tugged down Mateta, and the France striker made no mistake, burying the ball past Unai Marrero.

McNeil’s winner was the product of another acrobatic assist from fellow substitute Strand Larsen, whose scorpion kick teed up Pino at Coventry.

This time it was an overhead kick, which was heading wide of the goal but McNeil pounced at the post to poke it home.

Palace were awarded a second penalty when Soler was charged with a handball, but Marrero was equal to it, giving the visitors a fighting chance at a last-gasp leveller.

But Henderson produced his biggest save of the night, denying Orri Oskarsson at the death to preserve a much-needed Palace win.

Iran war oil shock drives dip in global emissions, study shows

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a latest study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.
  • It has been revealed that emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change.
  • "It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," mentioned the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Global carbon emissions are set to slightly drop this year, a latest study suggests, largely as a result of high energy prices in the wake of the US war on Iran and the disruption of supply through the Strait of Hormuz.

It has been revealed that emissions from oil, gas and coal are the main drivers of climate change. While over the past decade, these emissions have risen by 0.9% per year, they are expected to drop by 0.4% in 2026.

"It's downwards, which sounds good, but this is largely driven by the war in Iran, what's happened in the Strait of Hormuz," mentioned the study's co-author Glen Peters, a scientist at the CICERO Center for International Climate Research in Norway.

"So in a way, a little bit of good news, but for the wrong reasons.".

The study was released while global leaders are meeting in Turkey for the United Nations' COP31 climate conference.

Sources indicate that the study published by international research group the Global Carbon Project found that oil emissions dropped by 1.9% in 2026, while natural gas fell by 0.3%. Coal emissions however continued to rise, by around 0.6%.

"A drop in emissions in ‌one year is not a peak unless it ‌is driven ​by structural change," Peters cautioned.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that A structural change would mean that emissions would slowly rise to a peak and then slowly decline afterward, indicating a long term trend. That's not what happened though, Peters stated. "What we see this year is [that] oil emissions are going up and then suddenly, bang, down 2%.".

It is the third time in recent years that global carbon pollution has dropped. The previous declines were during the global economic crisis in 2009 and during the COVID pandemic in 2020. In each of those cases, emissions went back up once global economies recovered.

While the geopolitical shocks of the past year have been the driving factors behind the temporary emissions reversal, there has also been a rise in renewable energy contributing to the data. So while solar panels, wind farms and electric vehicles did make a difference, they were just not enough to cut emissions by themselves.

"The long-term answer remains the rapid deployment of clean energy technologies," according to co-author of the study, Pierre Friedlingstein, of the Global Carbon Budget Office at the University.

And even though emissions from fossil fuels dropped slightly, overall global carbon dioxide emissions still went up by about 1%, the study warns. The overall rise is because of land use changes like deforestation and peat fires, which increased too fast to be offset by the slight decrease in fossil fuel burning.

Hoping to create some separation in the top half of the Scottish Premiership table, Dundee United will welcome St Johnstone to Tannadice Park on Saturday.

The Tangerines could make it nine games unbeaten this weekend, while the Saints are keen to bounce back from defeat last time out.

Jim Goodwin's Dundee Utd have proven immensely resilient this term, and arrive full of confidence having lost just once on home turf in the league.

Adding to that feeling is the fact the Tangerines thrashed Hibernian 4-0 on the road last Saturday, thanks to a brace from Zachary Sapsford and second-half efforts from Lyall Cameron and Jesse Randall.

That victory has Goodwin's side fifth in the Scottish Premiership table with 20 points from their 13 matches, a tally that sees them three clear of city rivals Dundee in seventh having played one game fewer.

United will be aiming to distance themselves from the bottom half this weekend, though it is notable they have drawn as many matches as they have won in 2026-27, including three of their last five.

The hosts also kept just one clean sheet during that spell while conceding six goals in the process, letting in two in the 3-2 home win over Aberdeen, and two in the 2-2 stalemate at Celtic on October 28.

Meanwhile, Simo Valakari's St Johnstone are feeling the pressure from their rivals, and face a tough test to stay in the top half this weekend.

The Saints were downed 2-1 by Falkirk last Saturday, falling two goals behind shortly after the interval and only pulling one back late on through Josh Campbell.

That defeat brought a three-game unbeaten streak to an end, and means that Valakari's side arrive having triumphed in just one of their last six matches, beating Dundee 2-1 on November 7.

To make matters worse, St Johnstone failed to keep a clean sheet in any of those six clashes, conceding two or more on four separate occasions.

Right now sixth with 17 points after 14 games, the Saints will be looking over their shoulder given they are level with Dundee and just three points ahead of Aberdeen, Hibernian and 10th-placed St Mirren.

Knowing that they are at risk of dropping down into the bottom six, fans of the visitors will also be concerned after seeing their team score the fewest goals of any team in the top half (18).

By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 01:56.

Toulouse can potentially climb into the top half of the Ligue 1 table with a win over Rennes on Sunday at Stadium de Toulouse.

Both teams walked away with 1-1 draws the last time out, with Le Tefece sitting 12th after collecting a point versus Lens, putting them three points behind Rennes, who are ninth, after drawing Lorient.

For the second time domestically this season, Toulouse failed to emerge victorious last week when scoring first.

Those four points dropped represent the difference between their current position and a spot in Europe next season.

On the other hand, they have avoided defeat in seven of their last eight league games, including the last three at Stadium de Toulouse.

In their last three Ligue 1 home contests, this team have netted a combined six goals, six more than in their opening two games played in Toulouse.

Discipline has been an issue for Jens Berthel Askou’s men in the top flight this season, as they average the second-most fouls per match in the competition (15.7).

Toulouse can extend their Ligue 1 home unbeaten run versus Rennes on Sunday to five matches, last beating them in Toulouse in 2025 (2-1).

A campaign that began with so much promise has deteriorated for Stade Rennais, who have struggled to find consistency this month.

Franck Haise’s men are on a five-match winless run across all competitions, having begun 2026-27 unbeaten in their first five competitive fixtures.

A 3-1 loss at NEC in Europa League action on Thursday has them narrowly above the knockout stage line in that competition.

In November, they have netted a goal or fewer in each of their competitive games, while conceding a combined six times in their last three competitive outings.

Away from home, Rennes have really been exposed defensively in the league, conceding a combined 14 goals in their last four domestic matches as the visitors.

Les Rouge et Noirs are second in the league regarding expected goals, though they have conceded more penalties than anyone in the competition so far (five).

Rennes form (all competitions):.

Toulouse may be without Mark McKenzie, who suffered a hamstring strain in their last match, while Aron Donnum is eligible to return from his suspension.

Jacen Russell-Rowe netted for them in the opening half at Lens, his third of the Ligue 1 campaign, tied with Thomas Jorgensen for second on the team.

A minor knock has Valentin Rongier questionable in this outing for Rennes, while Adrien Thomasson will miss the match with a red-card suspension.

Boulaye Dia scored in their draw at arch-rivals Lorient last Sunday, putting him up to six in the league this season, one fewer than last season’s leading goalscorer in Ligue 1, Esteban Lepaul.

Toulouse possible starting lineup:.

Restes; Diallo, Koumbassa, Nicolaisen, Tape; Jorgensen, Casseres, Sigur, Russell-Rowe; Vignolo, Tengstedt.

Rennes possible starting lineup:.

Samba; Reynolds, Cresswell, Oliveira, Rouault; Cisse; Al-Taamari, Blas, Camara; Dia, Lepaul.

As much as they have struggled of late, we believe Rennes' firepower will be sharper this weekend and punish a Toulouse backline that is far from reassuring defensively.

Paul Pogba believes Manchester United should follow Arsenal’s blueprint under Mikel Arteta and has accused his former club of living in the past.

United decided to sack Michael Carrick during the international break and have brought in Mauricio Pochettino to deliver an immediate turnaround after a poor start to the season.

Pochettino suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat to Liverpool in his first game in charge and that was followed by a 2-2 draw away to Sporting CP in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

United have not won a trophy in their last two seasons and Pochettino’s side are now in an early relegation battle as they sit 19th in the Premier League with eight points from 11 games.

Pogba, meanwhile, has endorsed Pochettino’s move to Old Trafford but feels United need to look at Arsenal’s return to the top as a model to follow.

‘I’m happy that Pochettino has gone there because I think he’s a great manager. And I’m sad also for Michael Carrick because I don’t think he had enough time to show and prove himself,’ Pogba told talkSPORT.

‘But I think we just need to give time to this team. We know there’s a lot of fans all over the world and we all want Man United to win and we all think that they should change manager.

‘All I think about this team, I’ve been there, is that you need time, you need to fix the stuff inside.

‘Everybody needs to be in the same position and give time to the manager to do his things.

‘But the pressure, I know it’s a major club, it’s Manchester United, was way less. They let Arsenal make their own way back to the top.

By BEN WILLCOCKS, ASSISTANT SPORTS EDITOR and CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 04:00 EST, 26 November 2026 | Updated: 06:54 EST, 26 November 2026.

Manchester United legend Peter Schmeichel fears Senne Lammens has yet to recover from the blunder he made during Belgium's World Cup campaign last summer.

Lammens made two costly mistakes in United’s 2-2 Champions League draw with Sporting Lisbon on Wednesday night, conceding a needless penalty and dropping a clanger in the dying minutes to allow Luis Suarez to score twice for the home side.

The 24-year-old goalkeeper, who was one of Manchester United's standout performers last season following his £18.1million transfer from Royal Antwerp, has looked unconvincing so far this term and played a part in the club conceding more goals (35) than any other side in Europe's top five leagues.

Former Red Devils goalkeeper Schmeichel believes Lammens has never fully recovered from his error that led to Belgium being dumped out by Spain at the World Cup quarter-final stage last summer.

In the 88th minute of the match, with the score locked at 1-1, Lammens spilled the ball into the path of Mikel Merino, who tapped home to send Spain through to the semi-finals.

Asked if the confidence-shot goalkeeper should now be dropped by Mauricio Pochettino for Karl Darlow, who was signed by United in the summer, Schmeichel told CBS Sports: ‘I don’t know where that point is.

Senne Lammens made two big errors during Manchester United's 2-2 draw at Sporting Lisbon.

Peter Schmeichel fears Lammens has never fully recovered from his blunder at the World Cup.

‘Mauricio Pochettino has come in, he’s brought his own staff, that means he’s got a new goalkeeping coach and maybe that is something that can change it for him.

‘I don’t know if you remember in the World Cup, he came against Spain and made a bit of a mistake, Merino scored and they got knocked out, and I feel like he’s lost a little bit of confidence from that mistake, hasn’t really recovered.

‘As a goalkeeper when you’re not on your best form you need your defenders in front of you to help you out and the sad truth is that they haven’t been able to do that and of course, that makes it so much worse.'.

Joshua Zirkzee insists United’s players will rally around Lammens and won’t let their under-fire goalkeeper ‘suffer by himself’.

The two costly errors undid Lammens’ good work after he saved an earlier penalty from Suarez, but Zirkzee said the players are determined to support the Belgian.

Sources indicate that ‘This team is a family, so there's no one who will suffer by themselves,’ noted Zirkzee. ‘Mistakes happen. Let's go on to the next one. Senne’s a great goalkeeper.

Recent findings suggest that ‘In this moment, we just give him space. I’m not sure if he wants to hear anything at all. But Senne’s a great kid. He's got a good head on him and we all know that next game he is going to be at the top of his game. We didn't draw because of him. I'm also someone who likes to look at myself and, you know, I didn't score.’.

United had two goals disallowed by Polish referee Szymon Marciniak as well as conceding the two penalties and seeing Youri Tielemans sent off – three days after Leny Yoro was shown a controversial red card at Liverpool – and Zirkzee admitted that it feels like the world is against Pochettino’s team at the moment.

The Belgian shot-stopper conceded a needless penalty just minutes after saving a spot-kick.

He then spilled the ball into the path of Luis Suarez late on, gifting Sporting a late equaliser.

‘Yeah, we're in a place where it can feel like that pretty quick,’ he added. ‘But as I noted, we've got a locker-room that's built on supporting each other and we will get out of it eventually. If it's us against the world, so be it.

‘For the team that we are, we shouldn't really be looking at what the referee decides, but you cannot deny that it was some key decisions that weren't in our favour, to put it like that.

It has been revealed that ‘But, as I mentioned, we shouldn't really be looking at the referee. All we have to do is look at ourselves. In the end, I think we drew because of small details, little mistakes. But we definitely have something to build on, mainly the way we started the second half. I think that's something we can build on and move on with. Our team should be capable to win even if we're not being favoured in those moments.’.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Your weekly briefing on Tottenham, featuring team news and expert analysis from Sam Tabuteau.

Industry observers note that I would like to be emailed about offers, event and updates from Evening Standard. Read our privacy notice.

Sunday’s Premier League games will be kicking off at slightly weird times this weekend.

Tottenham and Liverpool will be affected, while Arsenal take on Manchester City in the normal 4.30pm GMT tea-time kick-off later in the afternoon.

Andoni Iraola’s Liverpool, fresh off their 4-0 win over fierce rivals Manchester United, are in Merseyside derby action against Everton.

Spurs take on Sunderland at the Stadium of Light, while Crystal Palace and Fulham are both at home, with Hull City and Bournemouth travelling to the capital.

Brighton and Hove Albion also take on Newcastle United at the Amex Stadium.

The two sides that have not had their kick-off time changed are Arsenal and City, who collide in a heavyweight clash at the Emirates Stadium, with neither side coming into it off the back of a victory.

The Gunners were held to a 1-1 draw by Borussia Dortmund in midweek, following on from their late 2-2 stalemate at Newcastle last weekend.

City, meanwhile, were also frustrated by Fulham at home and then drew 2-2 with Napoli in midweek.

The reason for the weird kick-off times this weekend is because there is no game on Saturday lunchtime.

That slot was supposed to be for Everton hosting Liverpool, but that game has been moved to Sunday, where the game will kick-off at 12pm GMT at the Hill Dickenson Stadium.

Because that match is kicking off at 12 noon, the 2pm kick-offs have been pushed back by five minutes to try and ensure that there is no overlap between the earlier fixture and the four afternoon games.

It also means that the 2.05pm matches are unlikely to clash with the 4.30pm game.

The Europa League and Conference League have also been a factor, with the English top flight stopping clubs from playing twice within 60 hours of each match.

As a result, Palace, Sunderland, Bournemouth and Brighton - all in action on the continent on Thursday - are obligated to play their next matches on Sunday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

A quick sprint, a well-placed pass and an instinctive finish. Bradley Barcola and Alexander Isak will have done this dozens of times in training but here, on a squally Sunday afternoon, this combination secured a little piece of history.

According to recent reports, anfield has witnessed plenty of significant goals down the years but never had this crowd seen one that cost £248m to make. Liverpool invested a near quarter-billion pounds on Barcola and Isak for bigger occasions than a tussle with Brighton and Hove Albion, but this rapid interchange felt like a significant moment.

Liverpool are a work in progress under Andoni Iraola but with each minute of each game you can see signs of things knitting together, and if Barcola and Isak are finding harmony, with Florian Wirtz in behind, then, perhaps, this journey will start to accelerate.

This was an vital afternoon for Liverpool’s head coach, a difficult assignment against high-flying, well-respected opponents in Brighton, who arrived on Merseyside having won their last four Premier League fixtures with a combined aggregate of 15-0, including a 3-0 thumping of reigning champions Arsenal.

Sources indicate that but Liverpool rose impressively to the challenge and there are grounds for saying this was the most significant success to date for Iraola, whose team defended relentlessly to preserve a clean sheet. They are up to fourth now after this 2-0 success and deserve their position.

“I’m very happy,” Iraola mentioned. “We faced a very good opponent, similar to Villarreal [in the Champions League]. It’s difficult to defend them a lot of times and it was key how we started. We needed to be aggressive, recover balls, win our duels, be dangerous in transitions: I think we’ve done it.”.

In a recent development, and how. Iraola was able to march towards the Kop at the end, to clap the supporters and acknowledge only Liverpool’s fifth (and his first) Premier League win at Anfield in 2026, and it was evident he had a spring in his step from what he had seen.

Whether the game would have flowed in the direction it did had Brighton taken the lead can only be speculated but what a glorious chance they wasted for us to find out: in the 13th minute, five swift, one-touch passes bamboozled Liverpool’s defence and created space for Yasin Ayari.

With the goal at his mercy, Ayari could have made things exceptionally uncomfortable but he leant back and blazed over. He clasped his face and grimaced, knowing what had gone begging in front of the Kop; four minutes later, his misery was exacerbated.

"He's GOT to hit the target!" Yasin Ayari missed a golden chance to put Brighton ahead against Liverpool 🫣 https://t.co/Qz7G3sXCpP.

Liverpool’s lead was secured with an element of good fortune but, equally, the tenacity of Ronald Araújo and Wirtz was instrumental in pressing Brighton back to the point that they were panicking; Wirtz’s shot, deflected off Pascal Gross past Bart Verbruggen, compounded it all.

“I think everyone in the stadium – and you as well – felt there was a missed opportunity for us,” groaned Fabian Hürzeler, the visitors’ head coach. “It’s not only after the goal or the goals they scored. Before they scored, we had two substantial chances. I think it was just the difference that they scored and we didn’t score.”.

It would be wrong to say Wirtz was doing cartwheels – perhaps he knew immediately he would not get the goal – but it was an key moment for him and you could feel the sense of goodwill towards him from team-mates and supporters alike.

Florian Wirtz's deflected shot has put Liverpool ahead minutes after Brighton had a great chance of their own ⚽️ https://t.co/b6mRvl2rSR.

Remarkably, this was the first time Liverpool had scored in the first half at Anfield in a Premier League fixture since May 9 and, with that momentum, it led to one of those periods when they started attacking in waves and carried the crowd with them.

What they needed was a second goal to arrive quite rapidly and that is what happened when Barcola won possession, scuttled forward and played a perfectly weighted bobbling ball into Isak’s path; the Swede did the rest, calmly finishing from eight yards.

Sources indicate that everything with Isak feels to be going under the radar at the moment, but that is six goals in six Premier League appearances. He is starting to show the consistency and killer instinct that everyone felt he would. Iraola will be hoping it continues for the foreseeable future.

Industry observers note that alexander Isak scores to double Liverpool's lead at Anfield! 💥 https://t.co/oYs2jnHZEb.

“The performance was really good,” remarked Isak, the quiet assassin. “We were really solid against a really good team. The first half is what we really want to be about. It was about intensity, winning balls and countering.”.

Brighton, as much as Hürzeler protested, could not properly recover, though this is no criticism. They remain committed to attack, they struck the frame of the goal when Ayari tried to punish an Alisson Becker mistake and the desire to keep pushing ensured Liverpool could never relax.

What Liverpool had going for them this time, however, was an intensity to preserve a clean sheet and nobody embodied the indefatigability more than Araújo, the Uruguay international whose loan from Barcelona is looking an increasingly shrewd piece of business.

Two moments stood out: one thunderous tackle on substitute Malick Yalcouyé in front of the Main Stand that had the locals roaring their approval, another in the first half when he was on the floor but still managed to head away to thwart Maxim De Cuyper.

They remember those moments as much as the stardust that Barcola and Isak provide. Put it all together and it might just be a launchpad for Iraola.

Iraola has his first Premier League home win in charge of Liverpool thanks to a 2-0 victory over Brighton. The hosts netted twice in the first half through Wirtz’s deflected strike off Gross and Isak’s close-range finish. This result moves Liverpool above Chelsea and up to fourth, just a point behind third-place Brighton, who suffer their first defeat in any competition since August 30.

Manchester United have held talks over a January move for Fulham defender Calvin Bassey.

United’s defence shipped another four goals last weekend against Liverpool with only Crystal Palace conceding more in the Premier League this season.

With the club slumped in 19th place after 11 games, Mauricio Pochettino will be backed in the January transfer window with a centre-half, a left-back and a striker targeted.

While they are also interested in Everton’s Jarrad Branthwaite and Brentford star Nathan Collins, Bassey has emerged as a leading target for United.

His current contract at Craven Cottage expires in the summer with Fulham holding the option to extend that by a further 12 months.

The Cottagers are also in active talks with their captain over a upcoming contract. But United remain hopeful of prising him away from west London with The Athletic reporting talks are taking place to ‘understand the conditions’ of a January move.

Bassey turned in another fine performance as Fulham held Manchester City to a 1-1 draw at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

Speaking after the game, the former Rangers star was asked about his future, telling TNT Sports: ‘Of course [it is something we want to get done quickly.].

Industry observers note that ‘We are negotiating, we are still talking. It’s an amazing place to be, I have settled in nicely and the manager has put a lot of faith and trust in me. It’s nice to be here and hopefully we will see what happens with the negotiations.’.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Auxerre will try to put some more distance between themselves and the relegation zone as they wrap up November by welcoming Marseille to Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps on Sunday.
  • After 11 matchdays, the Burgundy club sit 15th in the Ligue 1 table, drawing Monaco 1-1 the last time out, with OM currently in fifth following to a 3-2 defeat at Le Mans.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 27 Nov 2026 02:00.

Auxerre will try to put some more distance between themselves and the relegation zone as they wrap up November by welcoming Marseille to Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps on Sunday.

After 11 matchdays, the Burgundy club sit 15th in the Ligue 1 table, drawing Monaco 1-1 the last time out, with OM currently in fifth following to a 3-2 defeat at Le Mans.

After a rough start to the 2026-27 campaign, it appears as though Auxerre are doing just enough to get by domestically.

Will Still’s men lost their first three matches of this top-flight season, but have since collected points in six of their last eight league fixtures.

That has them just a point above Strasbourg who are in the relegation playoff spot heading into matchday 12 with Auxerre just three points above Angers, who are in the last automatic relegation position.

So far this season AJA have yet to lose a Ligue 1 fixture when netting the opening goal, with their draw versus Monaco last week being the first time they dropped points in that position.

They lead the league regarding fouls per match (16.1) while allowing the joint-most goals in this competition after 11 matchdays (25).

AJA have points in three of their last four Ligue 1 fixtures at home, with their last win at Stade de l’Abbe-Deschamps occuring in September against Brest (2-1).

Marseille will hope their late collapse against Le Mans serves as a temporary speed bump and a wake-up call going forward.

Bruno Genesio’s side bounced back well in midweek, defeating Levski Sofia 1-0 in Europa League action, putting them into the knockout places in that competition.

Clean sheets like the one they collected on Thursday have been rare for OM in Ligue 1, as they have conceded a 2.40 xG average following their defeat to Le Mans in the top flight.

Fortunately, they are balancing that out with plenty of goals, averaging the second-most goals per game in Ligue 1 (2.2) heading into matchday 12.

After 11 matchdays, only three points presently separate them from the top three and a place in next season’s Champions League.

Les Olympiens will seek a third successive triumph versus Auxerre in this competition, having won both Ligue 1 meetings against them last season 1-0.

Marseille form (all competitions):.

Both Bryan Okoh and Assane Diousse will miss this match for Auxerre as they recover from cruciate ligament tears, while Sekou Fofana has a groin strain and Danny Loader is questionable with an ankle injury.

Romain Faivre scored their only goal on matchday 11, the second of the campaign for the man currently on loan from Bournemouth.

At Marseille, Derek Cornelius is still recovering from a hip problem, Emerson Palmieri is questionable with a knee injury and Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg is questionable because of an illness.

Amine Gouiri scored the winner in their Europa League victory on Thursday, becoming the first OM player to net in five successive competitive fixtures since Florian Thauvin in 2018, while he and Igor Paixao scored in their defeat to Le Mans.

Auxerre possible starting lineup:.

Nardi; Diomande, Tuanzebe, Siwe; Senaya, Ahamada, Danois, Oppegard; Faivre, Lascary; Archer.

Marseille possible starting lineup:.

De Lange; Weah, Egan-Riley, Aguerd, Garcia; Kamissoko, Nnadi; Gomes, Maupay, Paixao; Gouiri.

These are two of the most inconsistent defensive units in the league, and in a match which could be wide open for that reason, we believe the quality of the visitors, who have fared well in those kinds of matches this season, will enable them to prevail.

Mikel Arteta’s side are well-stocked with options at right-back, with Jurrien Timber and Ben White both impressing so far this season.

However, while Timber is reportedly close to signing an extension on his current contract, Fresneda is seen as a potential successor to 29-year-old White, whose contract runs out in June 2028.

  • The Eagles came from behind after trailing to a second-half goal by Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Thomas Frank believes his first win as Crystal Palace manager can be a “turning point” in the club’s season.

Palace sit bottom of the Premier League table but tasted victory for the first time in Frank’s tenure with a 2-1 win over 10-man Real Sociedad in his second game in charge.

The Eagles came from behind after trailing to a second-half goal by Chelsea loanee Mamadou Sarr.

But Jean-Philippe Mateta levelled from the penalty spot after Jon Martin was shown a second yellow card and sent off for the side sat fifth in La Liga.

Palace then scored their eventual winner through substitute Dwight McNeil but almost threw it away when Dean Henderson was required to make a last-gasp save after Yeremy Pino had seen the Eagles’ second spot-kick of the night saved.

Palace’s victory came five days after their 3-2 defeat at Coventry in Frank’s first match in charge.

“In the second half I felt we kept the ball much better,” Frank noted after his side’s victory on Thursday.

Industry observers note that “What I really liked was the belief from the players. It is so key to keep doing the right things and keep believing.”.

Palace were guilty of giving the ball away in poor errors and handing Sociedad some cheap chances despite eventually closing out a victory.

Frank remarked: “We should just control that game. But we probably don’t have the confidence right now.

Asked whether the win against Sociedad can be a turning point in a so-far difficult season for the south Londoners, Frank replied: “I think it could be. But we need to follow it up, of course, with a good performance against Hull on Sunday. But there were a lot of positives from this game.”.

Arsenal host Manchester City on Sunday afternoon with Enzo Maresca’s side title hopes fading after a run of four games without a win.

Manchester United are sat in 19th place and host Brentford at Old Trafford in a huge game for Mauricio Pochettino after his debut in the dugout ended in a 4-0 humiliation at Anfield last Sunday.

Liverpool meanwhile make the short trip over to the Hill Dickinson Stadium for the first Merseyside derby of the season with Everton picking up just one win in their last 10 meetings with their neighbours.

As ever, England legend and Betfair ambassador Alan Shearer has revealed his Premier League predictions to Metro.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Chelsea are understood to be monitoring Boca Juniors centre-back Facundo Herrera after the defender’s swift emergence in South American football.
  • The 20-year-old, known in Argentina as ‘Jagger’ because of his likeness to Rolling Stones singer Mick Jagger, has made remarkable strides over the last four months.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 27 Nov 2026 02:11.

Chelsea are understood to be monitoring Boca Juniors centre-back Facundo Herrera after the defender’s swift emergence in South American football.

The 20-year-old, known in Argentina as ‘Jagger’ because of his likeness to Rolling Stones singer Mick Jagger, has made remarkable strides over the last four months.

After making his senior bow in August, the former captain of Boca’s reserve side swiftly established himself in the first team and helped the club win the Copa Sudamericana in Barranquilla last week.

Herrera impressed in the 2-0 final triumph over Atletico Mineiro, completing 56 of 58 passes and recording nine clearances as Boca kept a clean sheet.

Argentine publications El Crack Deportivo and Clarin via Sport Witness report that Chelsea scouts are closely assessing Herrera's physical and technical progress as part of the club’s continuing recruitment drive in South America.

The 1.80m right-footer has earned plaudits for his speed, aerial strength and composure when playing through the opposition’s press from the back.

Herrera showed his eye for a decisive moment on October 25 by scoring his first senior goal with a late winner against Independiente that secured Boca's place at the top of the annual league standings.

The youngster's growing standing has attracted praise from some of Argentina’s most respected figures: Boca's record appearance-maker Roberto Mouzo has likened him to 1978 World Cup winner Alberto Tarantini, while Oscar Ruggeri has called on national team manager Lionel Scaloni to give him senior minutes straight away.

In a recent development, chelsea are not the only club following the youngster. Barcelona are reportedly seeking scouting reports ahead of January, while Benfica, Borussia Dortmund and Porto have also been linked with him.

Despite increasing interest from England and elsewhere in Europe, a move to prise Herrera away from La Bombonera in 2027 is unlikely to be straightforward.

Boca president Juan Roman Riquelme is determined to keep the heart of his trophy-winning squad together as the club prepare for next year's Copa Libertadores.

Head coach Rodolfo Arruabarrena has also told the board he wants the defender to stay, praising his strength in one-on-one duels and his willingness to learn from more experienced team-mates.

Boca have yet to receive a formal offer or begin transfer talks, putting the club in a strong position to resist early approaches while Herrera continues to develop in Buenos Aires.

#152185. Tech Report: A gut–brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila

📅 27 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 27m • 📚 Deep Dive (5494 w)

Tech Report: A gut–brain sensory-motor circuit regulates sugar ingestion in Drosophila

📅 27 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 27 min read (5494 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~27 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bidirectional communication between the brain and digestive tract is critical for optimizing nutrient preference and food intake, yet the neural mechanisms that couple gut nutrient sensing with ingestive motor control remain poorly understood.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Bidirectional communication between the brain and digestive tract is critical for optimizing nutrient preference and food intake, yet the neural mechanisms that couple gut nutrient sensing with ingestive motor control remain poorly understood. Here we identify a gut–brain sensory-motor circuit that regulates sugar ingestion in flies. We show that the brain neurons that regulate food ingestion, IN1s1, receive excitatory input from enteric sensory neurons that penetrate the foregut epithelium and detect sugars in the gut lumen during ingestion. Functional imaging and connectome analyses reveal that IN1s integrate excitatory input from multiple sugar-sensing neurons, including enteric sensory neurons, and provide inhibitory output to enteric motor neurons that control the muscles at the entry of the crop—a stomach-like organ. During ingestion, IN1 activation suppresses these enteric motor neurons, relaxes the crop duct and promotes rapid transfer of food into the crop, thereby enabling sustained food intake. Together, our findings describe a gut–brain circuit that controls the motor activity of digestive tract muscles during feeding and suggest a circuit mechanism by which nutrient signals from the gut contribute to the dynamic regulation of food intake across metabolic states.

It has been revealed that X.C. and N.Y. designed the study. X.C. performed most of the experiments and analyses in Figs. 1–5 and Extended Data Figs. 1–13. X.C. also annotated IN1s in the FlyWire connectome. M.R.M. identified and characterized enteric neuron GAL4 lines from the Janelia FlyLight first-generation collection and conducted most parts of the immunohistochemistry in Extended Data Figs. 2 and 5. N.Y. and S.N.T. cloned the IN1 split-GAL4 and split-LexA constructs and generated the transgenic lines. S.G. conducted the blue food feeding assays.
